title: Link doubling gave no remote centroid delay above ten percent at leak 0.1 in two passive adult worm models
abstract: We tested remote response timing after each electrical link doubled in passive models of two partial adult worm maps. At leak 0.1, none of 1,702,273 and 2,281,069 eligible link and pair cases had an impulse centroid delay above ten percent. The largest delays were 6.52 and 4.66 percent. At leak 0.01, two and three cases passed ten percent. Equal link weights gave four and one cases at low leak and none at the other tested leaks. A five-cell example gives a 1.75 percent delay despite a positive change in the decay operator. An exact rank-one update and direct solves check the counts. The result concerns assumed passive circuits, not measured neuronal delays. Incomplete electrical maps and unknown conductance, leak and capacitance limit biological use. Code, source hashes, retrieval steps, a figure and aggregate results support reproduction. External data records are excluded.
